Subject: Packaging guidance — upgrade vs modular add-ons

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Cleared a few internal questions but product wants a clearer recommendation on packaging before procurement will sign off. Two quick asks: 

1) Were evaluating a jump from your Compact tier to something higher for around 50 concurrent users (chat-heavy). Is that better handled by upgrading the tier or staying Compact + adding the throughput add-on?

2) We need to understand downgrade flexibility: if usage dips in year 2, can we drop seats or throughput, and how are credits/prorations handled? Procurement also asked for an estimate of a multi-year discount level to include in the RFx.

Best,
Samantha Lee

Samantha@clearwave.com

Hi Samantha,

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick summary up front: for a chat-heavy 50 concurrent users, we typically recommend upgrading to the MidThroughput tier if you expect sustained higher P50 latency SLAs and want bundled KV cache / priority capacity. If the load is spiky and short bursts dominate, keeping Compact and adding the throughput add-on is often more cost-efficient.

I attached a short proposal (proposal_v2.pdf) and a feature matrix that maps which features live in which tier. Highlights:
- Tier upgrade (Compact -> MidThroughput): predictable latency SLOs, built-in caching, monthly seat discount starts at 10% for 12mo commit.
- Throughput add-on: billed by reserved tokens/hour, flexible to scale up/down but no downgrade credits inside a billing month.

Downgrade / credits: see Monica's note below for operational details — the short version: prorated credits are available on downgrades but limited to 1 eligible change per 6 months for seat/throughput reductions (to protect capacity planning). If you need more flexibility we can structure a laddered commit with a smaller base plus burst pool.

For multi-year discounts, we can provide a 15% discount for a 24-month committed contract on tier pricing, and add-on discounts vary by volume (Priyom can provide bands).

Ill let Monica add the operational detail and Priyom chime on pricing bands and DocuSign next steps. Ill also include the SOC2 pack link in the follow-up.

Next steps: Can we schedule a 30-min carve-out with procurement + engineering next week? If you share preferred times Ill lock it in.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Samantha,

Quick operational notes from CS/Infra side to help you decide: 

- MidThroughput tier includes: hot KV prefix caching (reduces token spend for repeated prompts), priority placement on nodes (lower cold-start variance), and automatic batching optimized for 1024-token windows. This is beneficial if your workflows have long sessions with context carried across turns.
- Compact + Throughput add-on: good for burst patterns; you keep the Compact runtime behavior (no hot prefix caching) and buy reserved throughput to smooth cost during spikes.
- Downgrades: we process prorated credits back to the next invoice; however, to maintain cluster stability we limit downgrade events to one per 6-month window for capacity allocations. Emergency exceptions can be reviewed but require 30-day notice and may incur a 10% operational adjustment fee.
- Quantization / model variants: we can pre-select a quantized variant to reduce cost by ~20% token-equivalent while preserving generation quality for most clinical summarization workloads; this is a configuration change, not a contract-level downgrade, so its flexible.

If youd like, I can run a short workload sim against your average session trace to show cost delta between the two options.

Hi Samantha (and procurement team),

Thanks for the clear asks — below is a straight-up trade-off table and our proposed concession to help legal/procurement move forward. I kept it brief so you can paste into an RFx.

Option A: MidThroughput tier, 24-month commit
- Discount: 15% off tier list (final)
- Downgrade flexibility: one eligible downgrade event per 6 months (prorated credit back to the next invoice). Emergency downgrades considered with 30-day notice + 10% operational adjustment fee.
- Benefits: priority capacity, built-in KV cache, lower P95 tail latency. Includes 2 onboarding SOW days.

Option B: Compact tier + Throughput add-on, 24-month commit
- Discount: 12% off base tier + 10% off throughput add-on (volume-dependent)
- Downgrade flexibility: monthly adjustments to reserved throughput allowed with prorated crediting, up to 2 adjustments per quarter (we limit abuse to protect capacity). Seat reductions still subject to 6-month window.

Concession: If ClearWave signs a 24-month agreement and accepts Option B, we can increase throughput add-on discount by 5% (effective combined discount ~15%) and provide a 60-day rollback window in year 1 for one throughput reduction without operational fee.

Procurement ops:
- DocuSign: we use standard e-sign flow; Priyom will send the DocuSign package (MSA + SOW + pricing exhibit) once the option is selected.
- Compliance: SOC2 pack is available here: https://drive.redwood.com/compliance/soc2/latest (link in attached proposal).

Next steps: Priyom, can you prepare two pricing exhibits (Option A, Option B + concession) and a DocuSign draft? Samantha/procurement, if you can confirm which option youd like by EOD Friday Ill prioritize the package.

Thanks,
